hypotheses.reasoning: Trigger: geo-cache restarted after a node replacement at 12:09:29 with no RDB snapshot, so it came back with 0 keys (#1402). Amplification: ingest-api's geo-cache miss ratio jumped from a 4% baseline to 95% and then 99%, and each miss now loads from events-db (#1450, #1498). That turns cache lookups into a stampede of point queries (SELECT * FROM events WHERE id = $1) on events-db. events-db then hit 497/500 connections with CPU at 100% (#1457, #1549), and its queries slowed to 3-8s (#1578, #1646, #1791). ingest-api queries timed out at 5s (#1614), and the gateway returned 504s (#1565, #1648). The trigger alone is survivable; the damage comes from the cache-miss fallback to the database. The status-poller timeouts against the deprecated legacy-inventory endpoint (#494 onward) are unrelated noise and not the cause.

Alternative reading: events-db itself ran out of connections and CPU, so it is the failing resource. But that saturation is downstream of the miss storm that began at 12:09:29, and events-db showed no anomaly before then, so it is not the origin.

verdict.recommendedAction: Restore the geo-cache hit rate and take load off events-db: warm the geo-cache (or restore it from a snapshot), and temporarily stop ingest-api from falling back to events-db on cache misses (shed or rate-limit those lookups). Once the cache is warm, confirm that events-db connections and CPU recover. Then enable RDB/AOF persistence so node replacements don't start cold, and add a limit or circuit breaker on the database fallback path. Separately, retire the status-poller calls to the deprecated legacy-inventory /v1/status endpoint.
